sn17.6:1.3: The phrasing here is odd, but the regular syntax in the two phrases (object in accusative, subject in nominative, verb in imperative), as well as the parallel phrasing in the next Sutta, argue against it being corrupt (as posited by Bodhi). I think the Buddha is quoting a curse, then he substitutes the Dhammic meaning. Compare Atharva Veda 8.4.20: “Let Indra hurl his lightning at the sorcerers!”, where Sanskrit _aśani_ = Pali _asani_ (“lightning-bolt”). See the next Sutta and note. | For _asanivicakka_ (“forked lightning”) see Rig Veda 4.35.2, where _vicakra_ means “divided”. This phrase is only used in one other place in the canon, which is also about a decadent monk ([dn25:11.3]()).
